_about: Chassis-side mounts for the suspension's inboard joints (PLAN s17 step C, D24). Geometry is generated by scripts/chassis_tabs.py from the hardpoints and the ghost chassis; Fusion builds it and the sweeps check it. LEFT side, mm; the right is the mirror. The chassis itself stays assumed context.

wishbone_tabs.basis: A double-shear tab pair at each inboard rod end (R-08): plates normal to the rod end's bolt axis, either side of the ball and its misalignment spacers (upright_design.json clevis.spacer_mm), running to the nearest chassis rail; each plate's round end is centred on the tube's axis, so it sits in the tube for the weld. The lower tabs are 40 mm wide: the leg's force runs across them, and 22 mm tabs bent to FoS 0.8 (HC-11)

rocker_bracket.basis: Two plates outside the rocker's pivot boss, held off it by 12 mm spacer tubes so they sit outside every rocker bolt stack, running down to an assumed rail below the pivot. The top rail (66 mm inboard) lies where the rocker's drop-link arm swings (+/-22 deg about the inboard side), so a bracket to it ran through that bolt's stack (code review); below the pivot nothing on the rocker swings

damper_tabs.basis: A double-shear tab pair at the damper's chassis eye, on the assumed cross tube below it. 8 mm round the bolt and leaning 12 mm towards the centreline, because the damper body starts 9 mm from the eye's centre (10 mm tabs straight down touched it in the pre-check). The damper's force is horizontal, across the tabs, so they widen to 36 mm 30 mm below the eye (a constant 16 mm tab bent to FoS 0.8, HC-11), leaning 25 mm away from the body so the wide part clears it; 35 mm made the left and right tabs meet at the centreline (sweep). 16 mm spacers either side of the eye, so the bolt stack sits outside the damper body's 40 mm width: the body starts 9 mm from the eye along its axis, so with 5 or 10 mm spacers the washers and head came within 1-1.5 mm of it and the ring spanner could not fit (fastener sweep)

context_cross_tube.basis: ASSUMED chassis member: the ghost chassis had no tube within 127 mm of the dampers' chassis eyes, so one cross tube between the top rails, under the eyes, is added to the context. It belongs to the chassis design, not this project. 25.0 mm, not the rails' 25.4, so the CAD union is not an equal-radius junction

context_rocker_rail.basis: ASSUMED chassis member: a short longitudinal tube 55 mm below each rocker pivot for the pivot brackets, clear of the drop link, the ARB lever and the pushrod. A chassis interface requirement, like the damper cross tube

rack_clevis.basis: Kaz rack: 1/4-28 internal threaded rack extensions with supplied aluminium clevises, 1/2 in slot, 0.325 in holes (kaztechnologies.com/steering-rack, read 2026-11-04). The kit's clevis does not suit the AM-M8T: its 1/2 in slot leaves no room for the 12 mm ball's misalignment spacers (the tilting rod end hit the ears in the pre-check), and its 1/4 in top hats do not fit the 8 mm bore. So the joint takes a custom 4130 clevis on the 1/4-28 extension, with a jam nut: slot 22 mm (ball + 5 mm spacer each side, as every other clevis here), 5 mm ears, M8 bolt. Its reach back along the rack is 4 mm so it clears the housing by more than 5 mm at full lock. Only the ears are modelled: the clevis's web behind the rod end needs about 25 mm between the joint's centre and the housing end at full lock, and the assumed housing leaves 20 mm, so the rack's extensions must be about 5 mm longer than assumed (an interface item: confirm against Kaz's drawing)

rack_brackets.basis: Kaz rack: 'adjustable aluminium trunnion blocks along the rack tubes' (no published size or pattern). Assumed: one block per side at 140 mm from the centreline, modelled as a collar round the rack housing (25 mm outside radius, 30 mm long), bolted by two M8 bolts to a 4 mm 4130N plate welded to the lower side rail (R-07)
